title: FHFA House Price Index — Quarterly Index with Monthly Tables (September 2027 and 2027Q3), 9:00 a.m. ET — inside the December FOMC communications blackout
source: FHFA: two FHFA primaries fetched direct 2026-09-08 by this session, independently of the sweep that proposed this id. (1) fhfa.gov/data/hpi (HTTP 200, 89,663 bytes) -- its 2027 HPI Release Dates table, ELEVENTH of twelve dated rows, reads verbatim 'Tuesday, November 30 | Quarterly Index (with Monthly Tables) | September 2027 and 2027Q3'; the same table marks exactly four 2027 rows quarterly -- February 23, May 25, August 31 and November 30 -- so the EDITION TYPE is the publisher's own label rather than an inference, and all twelve rows are last Tuesdays (Jan 26 -> Dec 28). (2) The published 2026Q2 report (HTTP 200, 1,522,949 bytes, released 2026-08-25; 517 stream objects located, 511 inflated in-session with node zlib and text-extracted from the Tj/TJ operators -- this runner has no pdftotext), whose 'FHFA HPI Release Dates for 2027' appendix page carries the identical row directly beneath the statement 'Public FHFA HPI(R) releases occur at 9AM ET and include a press release, tables, figures, and associated data' -- a published document rather than a second reading of the same web table, and the source of the 9:00 a.m. ET time. Promoted estimate -> confirmed on the precedent fhfa-hpi-2026-11-24, fhfa-hpi-2026-12-29, fhfa-hpi-2027-01-26, fhfa-hpi-2027-02-23, fhfa-hpi-2027-08-31, fhfa-hpi-2027-09-28 and fhfa-hpi-2027-10-26 set: the no-self-confirm limit binds the DISCOVERING sweep (fhfa-hpi-2027-10-26), not this event's own independent second look. THE PROPOSAL'S STATED REASON FOR STAYING estimate IS OUT OF DATE AND IS CORRECTED HERE: it wrote that this calendar's confirmed-tier prefixes have no member for a federal statistical agency's own posted forward calendar, but FHFA: is exactly that member, in the taxonomy at src/domain/market-events-data.ts line 51 -- 'fhfa.gov HPI release-date table + the published report's own notes' -- which is this pair of documents. 2027-11-30 is the last Tuesday of November 2027, its last calendar day, its last trading session, and a full NYSE session: Thanksgiving 2027 falls 11-25 and the half day 11-26. Checked 2026-09-08
notes: PROPOSED by the fhfa-hpi-2027-10-26 initial-research sweep (2026-09-06) as proposals/fhfa-hpi-2027-11-30.from-fhfa-hpi-2027-10-26.json and researched 2026-09-08; that proposal is now shadowed by this canonical file. All four of its instructions were followed and two of them changed the answer. INITIAL RESEARCH 2026-09-08 (docs/research/events/fhfa-hpi-2027-11-30.md). (1) THE STRUCTURAL FINDING THE PROPOSER ASKED FOR, CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: 2027-11-30 IS INSIDE AN FOMC COMMUNICATIONS BLACKOUT. The Board posted December 2027 as 12-07/08 (an SEP meeting); its blackout, derived from the Board's own rule, runs 2027-11-27 -> 2027-12-09, so this print sits inside it at D-7 to the decision. Across 56 posted meeting pairs 2021-2027 the last Tuesday falls in a blackout 7 of 7 in January, April, July and October, 0 of 7 in seven of the other eight, and 1 of 7 in NOVEMBER -- THIS IS THAT ONE. And because quarterly editions land only in February, May, August and November (0/7, 0/7, 0/7, 1/7), THIS IS THE ONLY QUARTERLY EDITION IN THE SEVEN-YEAR PANEL INSIDE A BLACKOUT. Independent corroboration: the derived start 2027-11-27 matches proposals/fomc-blackout-start-2027-11-27 exactly. It is not itself an FOMC day -- day one is 0 of 7 for November and day two is 0 of 67 post-policy releases. (2) BUT THE 10-26 SIBLING'S OCTOBER CONTROL MUST NOT BE IMPORTED HERE, BECAUSE THE DECEMBER BLACKOUT IS A DIFFERENT REGIME. The pooled result reproduces exactly (all blackout vs clear sessions, VIX9D/VIX 0.9884 vs 0.9065, p=0.0000, n=405 vs 1,020; 22 of 67 releases in blackout). December-meeting blackout sessions specifically (n=45) carry a COMPRESSED VIX RANGE -- 1.03 vs 1.59, p=0.0168 -- and only a weak front-end steepening (VIX9D/VIX 0.9600 vs 0.9269, p=0.0706; VIX close p=0.1029; SPX abs c2c p=0.9145). October's signature is the steepening; December's is the compression. The historical November sample cannot bridge them: 0 of the 5 post-policy November releases (2021-11-30, 2022-11-29, 2023-11-28, 2024-11-26, 2025-11-25) sit in a blackout, and all five are null on all four metrics (smallest p=0.7065). (3) THE CHAIN'S ONE INTRADAY RESULT DOES NOT SURVIVE AN EDITION SPLIT, AND THIS EVENT IS ON THE WRONG SIDE OF IT. Rebuilt from Yahoo 1h + includePrePost -- the 09:00 ET bar spans 09:00-09:30 and is FHFA-only -- over 727 sessions carrying that bar through 2026-09-04, containing 34 release mornings. The pooled reading reproduces (abs return 3.70 vs 8.64 bps, p=0.0201; range 30.78 vs 52.89, p=0.0299; signed p=0.6564). SPLIT BY EDITION: MONTHLY mornings (n=22) are the quiet ones -- 2.54 vs 8.64 bps, p=0.0223, seed-stable 0.0219-0.0224 -- while QUARTERLY mornings (n=12), this event's kind, read 6.34 vs 8.64 at p=0.4610 (seed-stable 0.4603-0.4614), p=0.2247 against the monthly editions and p=0.6609 against the tightest control of other late-month Tuesdays. On range neither sub-class clears alone (Q 0.1255, M 0.0912) although the pooled does -- a power statement, labelled as one. The sibling's finding is NARROWED, not overturned, and the narrowing removes a reading from this date rather than adding one. (4) CONTENT -- THE RESTATEMENT, MEASURED ACROSS 49 REPORT VINTAGES INSTEAD OF ONE. 50 archived report PDFs (2022-06-28 -> 2026-08-25) were downloaded and 49 parsed; each carries up to five (Previous Estimate) rows, giving 245 U.S.-column revision observations, of which the second-newest 1-month row is that report's FIRST restatement of the figure its predecessor first printed -- n=49 independent first restatements. Median absolute first restatement 0.10pp, mean 0.061pp, max 0.20pp, 21 of 49 unchanged, decaying by vintage (mean 0.061 -> 0.039 -> 0.024 -> 0.020 -> 0.024). ZERO SIGN FLIPS IN 49; of the 33 whose prior estimate was positive, 2 restated to zero-or-below and both were +0.1% -> 0.0%. AND THE QUARTERLY EDITION DOES NOT RESTATE HARDER THAN A MONTHLY ONE: median absolute first restatement 0.100pp for both, permutation p=1.0000 -- the direct answer to the proposal's question, and a counter-intuitive one. This is a different design from FT-fhfa-hpi-2027-08-31-5, whose n=50 was five vintage rows by ten cross-sectionally correlated census-division series FROM A SINGLE REPORT; both agree on the headline. The floor is disclosed: FHFA prints m/m to one decimal, so 0.1pp is the measurement quantum. (5) THE SEASONAL QUESTION WAS NOT RE-OPENED, per the proposal's instruction. September as a reference month is reported as context only (13/14 positive since 2012 at a +0.4962% median, 29/35 all-time, p=0.7726 since 2012 and p=0.9897 all-time, and the most recent September, 2025, printed -0.016%). The print's own headline, 2027Q3 q/q, is registered instead: Q3 is 13/14 since 2012 and 30/35 all-time, the ONLY non-perfect quarter and the widest all-time null of the four (p=0.8992 / 0.9937), against Q1 15/15, Q2 15/15 and Q4 14/14. The 142-observation quarterly series (1991Q1 -> 2026Q2, last SA 435.69) and the 426-observation monthly series (ending 442.53) both reproduce the 08-31 sibling to the cent. Live regime: last 12 quarters 12 of 12 positive at a +0.907% median but decelerating (2026Q1 +0.567%, 2026Q2 +0.348%); last six monthly m/m 4 of 6 positive at a +0.084% median. IMPACT STAYS low. symbols: [] and 0 hits for any housing, house-price or macro keying in trade-playbooks.md or multi-symbol-sweep.md (re-grepped 2026-09-08); nothing here licenses an entry.
